thread:
olivia: Heads up — getting multiple customer reports of 502/504 from hosted completions around 09:12 UTC. Latency also spiking. Gateway logs show memcached connection resets: "memcached: recv failed: connection reset by peer". Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/requests?range=15m needle: 502-rate up 8x. Can oncall triage?

samir: On it. Any request IDs or example curl so I can repro locally?

olivia: Example curl I just grabbed from a repro customer:
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions" \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"test"}'
```
Response: 502, body: "upstream read timeout". Gateway log excerpt: 
```
[gateway] 2026-03-17T09:12:21Z req=abc123 upstream=memcached-pfx-3 err=recv failed: connection reset by peer
[gateway] 2026-03-17T09:12:21Z req=abc123 status=502 latency=1123ms
```

mia: Seeing the same in infra metrics — memcached pool pfx-* has elevated connection errors and ~20% higher latency. Cache hit rate unchanged, but connection churn up. I just paged the memcached autoscaler on host pool pfx-3. Will check kernel/network errors.

dan: Several enterprise customers (acct: nordlabs, etherapps) already opened support tickets. Suggest messaging account leads and offering short credits if we cross SLO. I'll draft a quick note. @olivia can you add list of request IDs from customers?

olivia: Added a couple req ids to the ticket: abc123, def789, ghi456. Also saw a pattern where requests with prefix-key lookups are the ones failing more often.

samir: Repro locally by running a small flood of prefix-lookup requests — I can trigger memcached conn resets in staging with the same traffic profile. Steps: 1) run 500 parallel requests to /v1/completions with same prefix header; 2) watch gateway logs; 3) tail memcached logs on pfx nodes.

mia: Quick mitigation: switching gateway to bypass prefix caching for offending route. Doing a rolling config patch now (canary 10% first). If that brings 5xx down, we'll plan a longer-term fix (memcached pool repair + autoscaler tuning).

cache-monitor-bot: ALERT: memcached pfx-3 connection error rate > 1000/min, pool marked UNHEALTHY, restarting service on host pfx-3.

samir: Thanks — running a curl test against canary gateway (10%): got 200s consistent for ~50 requests, still occasional 502s for requests routed to pfx-3. Mia any ETA on pfx-3 restart?

mia: Restart in progress, checking for OOMs and tcp_reset counters. Initial kernel logs show no OOM, but netfilter dropped packets spike at 09:11. I asked infra to check network interface on host rack-7.

deploy-bot: Rolling deploy: gateway-config v2026.3.17-171 -> bypass prefix-cache on route /v1/completions (canary=10%). Release ID 9243.

olivia: Noting customers notified in ticket. Some ask for post-mortem and whether we triggered any automated retries that could have exacerbated load.

dan: On the customer side, they reported errors around 09:11-09:13 UTC and then again ~09:20. I'll escalate to acct leads and include short-term credits pending incident review.

mia: pfx-3 service restarted successfully at 09:18. Connection error rate fell to baseline in 2 mins. Can confirm netfilter counters reset after restart.

cache-monitor-bot: INFO: memcached pfx-3 pool restored. error_rate -> baseline within 120s.

samir: After canary ramp to 100% (v2026.3.17-171), 5xx rate back to normal. Running longer load tests now.

olivia: Customer-facing ticket updated with timeline and mitigation (bypass cache + memcached restart). Will ask for PRA (post-incident review) and include repro steps from samir.

mia: Action items: 1) investigate root cause of conn reset (kernel vs memcached), 2) add more aggressive memcached health-checking & failover to redis fallback, 3) tune autoscaler thresholds to avoid pool thrashing. I'll open infra follow-ups.

dan: I'll prepare credits and comms once PRA draft's available. Reach out if any customers still seeing issues.

olivia: Thanks team :thumbsup: — closing thread once PRA linked.
